newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares finish up on interest rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares finish up on interest rate hopes.

text.p: Italian shares closed higher across the board on Tuesday on a surge of domestic and foreign buying spurred by hopes of a discount rate cut by the Bank of Italy and an upbeat mood on Wall Street after the release of benign U.S. inflation data.

The blue chip Mib30 index burst through the psychologically significant 18,000 level to close at 18,328, a gain of 2.29 percent on the previous session. The all-share Mibtel index ended 2.08 percent higher at 12,320.
Bellwether stocks ENI and Fiat were in particularly strong demand, rising 3.31 percent and 3.82 percent to close at 8,735 and 5,850 lire respectively.
Traders said VW's recent strong performance in Germany was spilling over into other prominent auto stocks, among them Fiat.
Shares in Mediobanca and BCI surged ahead, boosted by rumours that the two banks are actively considering a full-blown merger of their operations.
Mediobanca finished 6.51 percent higher at 11,072 lire while BCI jumped 5.03 percent to 3,695 lire.
Olivetti was another big gainer, its shares leaping 4.54 percent to close at 554.6 lire.
With the political scene relatively quiet after last week's drama, market watchers saw shares continuing to firm until next week's preliminary consumer price data are out.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said earlier on Tuesday that he sees consumer price inflation falling below two percent year-on-year in April.
